question: Ascent, 5v5, round start (58s). Your team opens a default toward A. You are Cypher lurking Mid Bot. How do you play your lurk?

options.label: Plant a Trapwire at CT Mid, stay passive, wait for the A hit to pull DEF attention before making your move
options.explication_courte: The lurk pays dividends when the team engages on the opposite side: patience plus the trap secures rotation intel and lets you strike when DEF commit to A.

options.label: Take Mid control early with a Cyber-Cage to open a second threat (A split via Mid) and put DEF in a dilemma
options.explication_courte: Taking Mid creates a double-threat and generates info, but you become visible early and lose the surprise element that makes a lurk valuable.

sources_option.citation: Taking mid control opens split options and forces defenders to respect a second lane, but it commits you and reveals your position earlier.

options.label: Push Mid aggressively solo to fish for a pick in the first 20 seconds
options.explication_courte: Pushing too early solo turns the lurk into a blind duel: without team distraction at A, DEF can focus Mid and punish the premature push.

sources_option.citation: Ideally you wait at least 30 seconds before pushing; lurking too early, before your team draws attention, isolates you into a bad duel.

options.label: Abandon the lurk and join the A hit with the rest of the team for a 5-stack on site
options.explication_courte: Abandoning the lurk for a 5-stack removes the flanking threat and all rotation intel: DEF can rotate freely knowing only one axis is threatened.

sources_option.citation: A lurker's value is the backline pressure and flank threat; collapsing into the main group removes exactly the reason to lurk in the first place.

explication_longue:
Situation: Ascent, 5v5, round start (58s). Your team opens a default toward A. You are Cypher lurking Mid Bot, with Trapwire, Cyber-Cage, Spycam. Five DEF alive, positions unknown.

A lurk generates value two ways: (1) creating a split that forces DEF to choose between A and Mid, or (2) punishing a rotation with a high-value pick when DEF commit to one side. Cypher's Trapwire is the perfect passive sentry: plant it at CT Mid for free rotation intel without giving away your position.

Correct sequence: plant the Trapwire, stay passive, wait. When your team opens A and DEF rotate from CT Mid, the Trapwire reveals the rotator and you take the pick on a moving defender. Taking Mid control early (acceptable) creates a real double-threat but burns your surprise. Aggressive early push (costly) is the most common lurk mistake: without team distraction, DEF focus Mid and punish you. Joining the 5-stack (mistake) eliminates the flanking threat entirely.

Estimated elite distribution: ~55% passive Trapwire + wait for rotation, ~22% early Mid control, ~16% aggressive early push (costly), ~5% join 5-stack (mistake).

sources.citation: Wait at least 30 seconds before pushing; lurking is most effective when your teammates create distractions on the opposite side of the map.
Patience is the cornerstone of lurking; hit the enemy when they're most vulnerable, typically when focused on your teammates elsewhere.
A lurk wins by cutting rotations and applying backline pressure while the main hit forces the defenders to commit their attention.

_gaps.incertitude: Prendre Mid (acceptable) peut etre optimal dans une compo orientee Mid-control (Ascent) ; la frontiere depend du call d'equipe (default A pur vs A+Mid split) non entierement fixe par l'enonce.
Estimations depuis guides lurk (tracker, wecoach, note.com) ; aucun dataset public sur la frequence lurk-passif vs Mid-take par elo en elite.
